node.title: Re^3: Logic Help - Output to csv
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I have no idea what you did but it gives me a place to start and learn.

Yes, [mod://XML::Rules] does take a bit of studying its docs to understand all the rules. As for my [mod://XML::LibXML] [id://11117789|code], I hope that's a bit more clear. If you add use Data::Dump; at the top and add a dd \%items; just after the loop, you'll see the data structure:

{ "00123" => { "File 1" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", "File 2" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", }, "00124" => { "File 1" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", "File 6" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", }, "00125" => { "File 2" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", "File 7" => "www.site.com/path/to/file/file.pdf", }, }

The other tricky bit is the line that generates the @columns array. It has two main parts: map {keys %$_} values %items takes the [doc://values] of the %items, which are hashes themselves ({ "File 1" => "www..." etc.), and then uses [doc://map] to get the [doc://keys] of each of those hashes. In other words, the map statement will return the list "File 1", "File 2", "File 1", "File 6", .... The second part is the keys %{{map {$_=>1} ...}}, which is an idiom to get only unique values from a list. It does this by first building an anonymous hash with {map {$_=>1} values}, and then immediately dereferencing the hash (%{...}) and getting its [doc://keys]. Then, all that's left to do is [doc://sort] the unique strings.

I’m trying to print this out to a file but I’m getting errors about print usage.

What [hippo] [id://11117806|said]: first, you're opening the file for reading instead of writing. Second, note that the first argument of $csv->print should be the filehandle, which you did, but note that I was getting the output filehandle (STDOUT by default) using [doc://select], so you need to remove that call. This works for me:

open my $fh, ">:encoding(UTF-8)", "output.csv" or die "output.csv: $!"; my $csv = Text::CSV->new({binary=>1, auto_diag=>2, eol=>$/, always_quote=>1 }); $csv->print($fh, ["sku", @columns]); for my $sku (sort keys %$itms) { $csv->print($fh, [$sku, map { $itms->{$sku}{$_} } @columns ]); } close $fh;
